name: Mr. D Math
line: Mr. D Math is a teacher-led course in a fixed order. AMP chooses each problem from the last answer.
description: AMP vs Mr. D Math: a teacher-led video course in a fixed order, or practice chosen from each answer, explained at once and reviewed on a schedule.
verdict: Mr. D Math gives a learner a human math teacher, live classes for those who want them, and courses through Calculus I that its site says satisfy homeschool diploma requirements [1][2][7]. Its lessons follow a fixed order, and a self-paced student checks each worksheet against the key after finishing it [9]. AMP chooses every problem from the learner's answers, explains each one the moment it is answered, and brings old skills back on a schedule.
theirs: Mr. D Math is an online math school for grades 5 to 12, run by Dennis DiNoia, who has held Florida secondary math certification since 1988 [1][8]. It sells 5th grade math and Preparing for Pre-Algebra through Calculus I, plus Consumer Math, a Fractions Bootcamp and SAT and ACT prep, next to electives this page does not cover [2][5][9]. Its login and course catalog sit on the Edu20 platform [1][3].

Each course comes self-paced or live, and in a gamified version with points, badges and level-ups or a traditional one [5][11]. A self-paced lesson goes in four steps: watch the recorded lesson, work a worksheet of about 20 questions, check it against the solution key, then take a computer-graded quiz of about 5 questions [9]. Live students also join one 55-minute Zoom class a week [9].

The home page says the courses satisfy homeschool diploma requirements and support independent study for charter school and co-op students [1]. Families buy directly, and charter schools and grant programs that approve the vendor can pay for it [3][6].
credit: A human teacher. Live students get a weekly 55-minute class, and all students get live help sessions, three a week for live courses and two for self-paced [4][9]. Its site says email replies usually come within two hours [7]. AMP has no live teacher or tutor.
Credit for a transcript. Its site states WASC accreditation [1], and a charter school lists its live math courses for NCAA and A-G credit [5][10]. AMP offers no accreditation or course credit.
Calculus I and SAT and ACT bootcamps [2][9]. AMP stops at precalculus.
Vendor status with charter schools and grant programs, with separate course catalogs for some charter schools [3][6]. AMP's education-fund purchases cover three state programs.
A lower price for a single self-paced course: $247 for 2026–27, by one review's count [9].

reasons.title: Every answer is checked and explained at once
reasons.body: In a self-paced Mr. D Math lesson, the student works a worksheet of about 20 questions and then checks it against the solution key [9]. The keys show each step, color-coded to help find errors [10], and the student checks their own work against it [9]. AMP marks each answer the moment it is given, shows the correct answer and the worked steps, and offers a one-step hint beforehand that never gives the answer away.

reasons.title: The next problem fits the learner, not the syllabus
reasons.body: Mr. D Math's FAQ links a course-selection guide to help a family pick a course [4]. Inside the course, every student works the same lessons and the same printed worksheets; we found no adaptation within a course in its published materials [4][9][10]. AMP keeps a separate level in each of 14 strands of math and chooses every next problem from the learner's answers: new work, a prerequisite, or review.

reasons.title: A gap sends practice back to its foundation
reasons.body: In Mr. D Math, help with a stuck topic comes from live help sessions, two or three a week, or from email [4][7]. Its core courses start at grade 5 [2]. In AMP, two misses in a row on a skill send practice to what that skill builds on, on one map that starts at counting. Nobody has to notice the gap or book a session first.

reasons.title: Old skills come back on a schedule
reasons.body: Mr. D Math builds spiral reviews, mid-chapter reviews, chapter tests and semester exams into each course [9]. We found no review scheduled by time since a skill was learned. AMP brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics, and a miss starts the schedule over. In a randomized trial with seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice beat practice in blocks on a test a month later [16].

reasons.title: More practice, and paper made for one learner
reasons.body: One review of Mr. D Math notes that students who want a lot of practice may need a supplement [9]. Its worksheets are printed from the course, with an optional printed binder, and we found nothing made for the individual student [4][9][10]. AMP generates each problem fresh, so there is always another one, and it prints unlimited workbooks built from the learner's own record, each with a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

reasons.title: One license covers counting through precalculus
reasons.body: Mr. D Math sells each course separately, and a self-paced course stays open until March 1 of the next school year, with a $25 fee to extend it [4]. An AMP license covers every level AMP teaches, with no course to buy or renew when a learner moves up a level. A learner ahead in geometry and behind in fractions practices both in the same place.

rows.price: No prices on the pages we read [2][3][4]. One review lists $247 per self-paced course for 2026–27, and $247 plus a $290 live fee for a live year [9].
rows.buyers: Families directly, and students at charter schools and grant programs that list it as a vendor [3][6].
rows.range: Grade 5 and Preparing for Pre-Algebra through Calculus I, plus Consumer Math, a Fractions Bootcamp and SAT and ACT prep [2][9].
rows.start: The family picks the course, with a course-selection guide linked from its FAQ [4].
rows.teaching: Recorded video lessons in its own method. Live courses add one 55-minute Zoom class a week [7][9][10].
rows.next: The next lesson in a fixed course order. No adaptation within a course found in its published materials [4][9].
rows.mastery: No mastery rule stated. Grades come from computer-graded quizzes, chapter tests and semester exams [9]. Quizzes may be retaken with notes [11].
rows.review: Spiral and mid-chapter reviews built into the course [9]. No review scheduled by time interval found.
rows.print: Worksheets and answer keys printed from the course, or an optional printed binder. Nothing personalized per student found [4][9][10].
rows.adult: Prints worksheets and may check work against the keys. For live students, instructors grade assigned work [9][10].
rows.reports: Computer-graded quiz, test and exam scores [9]. No parent dashboard described in its published materials.
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site. No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [13][14].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Mr. D Math, randomized or with a comparison group, on its site. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [13][14].

The company describes its results without measuring them. Its home page speaks of a "high completion rate" and gives no figure [1]. Its reviews page offers six blog testimonials, with no scores, completion rates or sample sizes [12]. None of this compares students who took the courses with students who did not.
ours: Mr. D Math teaches first and practices after. AMP spends the learner's time on problems and brings the explanation to each one. In an online psychology course for adults, students who did more interactive activities learned more than students who watched more video or read more; the authors put the benefit of extra doing at more than six times that of extra watching or reading, in data that are correlational [15]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [16]. We expect a program that applies both at every problem to show it in outcomes. That is our bet, and we have committed to testing it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each is registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your teen wants a live teacher, a weekly class and someone to email with questions.
You need course credit for a transcript, or NCAA-approved live math courses.
Your student is ready for Calculus I.
Your charter school or grant program lists Mr. D Math as a vendor and will pay for it.
amp: Your child is not yet in grade 5, or has gaps from earlier grades. AMP starts at counting.
You want each answer checked and explained the moment it is given.
You want old skills to come back on a schedule, without planning it.
Your learner is ahead in one part of math and behind in another.
You want more practice than a worksheet holds, and paper made for your learner when you want it.

questions.question: Is Mr. D Math cheaper than AMP?
questions.answer: For one self-paced course, yes. The Mr. D Math pages we read show no prices [2][3][4]; one review lists $247 for a self-paced course in 2026–27, and $247 plus a $290 live fee for a live year [9]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child and covers every level from counting through precalculus.

questions.question: Does Mr. D Math give high school credit?
questions.answer: Its site states WASC accreditation and says its courses satisfy homeschool diploma requirements [1]. A charter school lists its live math courses for NCAA and A-G credit [10]. AMP offers no accreditation or course credit; it gives progress reports and report cards.

questions.question: Does AMP have live teachers like Mr. D Math?
questions.answer: No. Mr. D Math offers a weekly live class and two or three live help sessions a week [4][9]. AMP has no live teachers; it gives a one-step hint, a written lesson with a worked example and worked steps for every problem, and narrated films for a growing share of problem types.

questions.question: Can we use AMP alongside a Mr. D Math course?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP is a separate program. It finds the level in each strand of math within the first 24 problems, then chooses practice and brings earlier skills back for review.

questions.question: Is AMP proven to work better than Mr. D Math?
questions.answer: Not yet. We found no outcome study of Mr. D Math [13][14]. The evidence section above says where each product stands.
